External / portable drive · Water, fire or physical damage

Water, Liquid or Fire Damaged External Drive

Liquid can short the bridge board and the drive's own board, and corrosion starts quickly. Fire and heat can warp parts. Powering it on can destroy what is left, so keep it off and get professional help.

5/5 · Pro territory
Success odds: Low

Power, heat or opening the case can turn damage that could be fixed into permanent loss.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not plug it in or power it on, not even once to test.
  • Do not dry it with a hair dryer, oven or heater, and do not put it in rice. Heat can warp parts, and rice adds dust without drying the inside.
  • Do not open the drive or try to clean the disk.
  • Do not shake it or rinse it to remove dirt or salt.

Your steps

0 of 5 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Pull out the USB cable and any power adapter.
    2. Do not plug a wet adapter into the wall. That is a shock risk.
    3. Do not press any buttons to test it.
  2. Show me how
    1. Write down whether it was clean water, salt water, a sugary drink, flood mud, smoke or flames, and when.
    2. Take a photo of the drive as it is now, if safe.
  3. Show me how
    1. Leave the drive in its case, exactly as it is.
    2. Do not wipe or rinse it.
  4. Show me how
    1. Wrap it in a soft cloth and put it in a padded box.
    2. If it came from a flood and is muddy or salty, put it in a sealed plastic bag and keep it damp instead of letting it dry.
  5. Show me how
    1. Search for data recovery labs that use a cleanroom and ask for a quote before shipping.
    2. Ask about their price and their policy if they cannot recover anything.
    3. Send it with tracking and insurance.

Questions people ask

Can rice dry out a wet external drive?

No. Rice does not remove moisture well and can add dust. Keep the drive off and get professional help.

It only got a splash. Can I try it once it dries?

It is a gamble. Residue can short the board and a power-up can scratch the disk, so use a professional for important data.

Will the case protect the drive?

Not against liquid. Most cases are not sealed, and water can reach the board and the drive.
